'''Nar Hida''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Homeworld/Legends|hailing]] from the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Luptoom]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], he traveled to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] with his [[Nar Hida's wife|wife]] and [[Nar Hida's daughter|daughter]], where he opened a boutique that specialized in Luptoomian [[Clothing/Legends|fashion]]. Poor sales, however, forced Hida to close his store, and further dealings with local criminals left him and his family in a state of poverty. Hida intended to return to Luptoom, but the Separatist Crisis made leaving Coruscant particularly difficult.

He eventually found passage on the [[AA-9 Coruscant freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Jendirian Valley/Legends|''Jendirian Valley'']] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], but he soon discovered that the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] would only be traveling halfway to Luptoom. Fearing that he and his family would be left stranded without funds or [[Transport/Legends|transport]], Hida attempted to rob one of the ''Jendirian Valley''{{'s}} passengers during the journey. He was stopped by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was protecting [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. The senator gave Hida [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and suggested that he contact the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. With the movement's help, he and his family were able to return to Luptoom, where Hida reversed his fortunes.

==Biography==
===Failed business and destitution===
[[File:Coruscant-EotE.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Nar Hida relocated to Coruscant.]]
Nar Hida was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] who [[Homeworld/Legends|hailed]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Luptoom]], where he lived with his [[Nar Hida's wife|wife]] and [[Nar Hida's daughter|daughter]]. Looking for a challenging enterprise to pursue, Hida and his family relocated to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]],<ref name="db" /> which threatened the stability of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> There, Hida opened a boutique that specialized in fashions from his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], but within a year, he was forced to close the store due to poor sales. He made several business deals with the [[Baath brothers/Legends|Baath brothers]], but the deals only lost Hida more and more money, until he and his family were destitute. He intended to return to Luptoom somehow, but the [[Politics/Legends|political]] climate of the time made leaving the galactic capital difficult.<ref name="db" />

===The ''Jendirian Valley''===
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> Hida was able to secure passage for his family and himself aboard the [[AA-9 Coruscant freighter/Legends|AA-9 Coruscant freighter]] [[Jendirian Valley/Legends|''Jendirian Valley'']], with the last of his funds. The craft was the only one departing Coruscant that was not already packed to the brim with other refugees, but it was only traveling halfway to Luptoom, as Hida discovered. This worried Hida, as he and his family would be left stranded and broke by the time the ''Jendirian Valley'' had finished its journey. When the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] entered [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], the Luptoomian grew more and more desperate. Although he had never entered into criminal acts before in his life, he began to consider doing something drastic to turn his fortune around.<ref name="db" />

Presented with the opportunity of robbing a sleeping [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] passenger on the ''Jendirian Valley'', Hida only hesitated momentarily. As he moved to do the deed, he was grabbed on the arm by a young man and pulled aside.<ref name="db" /> The man was actually the disguised [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was traveling from Coruscant incognito.<ref name="blog">{{Blog|narbflick|9|Nar Hida: The Story Behind the Story}}</ref> He told Hida that the Bith was carrying a hidden [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and would have surely used it had the Luptoomian been allowed to follow through on his intended course of action. Hida was reluctant to believe the man but was convinced by Skywalker's companion, who was in fact [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], also in disguise. She told him to trust Skywalker as the young Jedi had the power to [[Force vision/Legends|see things before they happened]].<ref name="db" />

[[File:Anakin_and_Padme_refugees.png|thumb|left|350px|Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala (pictured) inspired Hida to donate to the Refugee Relief Movement.]]
Amidala then donated some [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to Hida and instructed him to contact the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], where the freighter would be stopping. Upon reaching the planet, Hida did as Amidala had told him, and the movement arranged for him and his family to be relocated to Luptoom. Back on Luptoom, Hida was able to build himself up out of poverty and turn his fortunes around. When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|broke out]] later<ref name="db" /> in 22 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]],<ref name="nec" /> Hida continually donated to the Refugee Relief Movement, inspired by the young couple that had helped him on the ''Jendirian Valley''.<ref name="db" />

==Personality and traits==
Nar Hida would never balk at the prospect of a challenge, but his enthusiasm in tackling the Luptoomian boutique in particular cost him dearly. He and his family were forced to live in poverty due to his business decisions and associations, and he was only able to alter his situation by relying on the kindness of others. In a moment of desperation, his mind turned to crime, and he would have committed robbery had he not been stopped by Skywalker. The kindness of the Jedi and Amidala would later inspire Hida to help people that found themselves in the position he had been in during the Separatist Crisis. He had [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and light skin.<ref name="db" />

==Equipment==
On the ''Jendirian Valley'',<ref name="aotc" /> Hida wore flowing, green [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] that had [[Limb/Legends|tentacle]]-like appendages around the chest and shoulder area.<ref name="cswe">{{CSWECite|II|39|Hida, Nar}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Creation and filming===
[[File:Freighter_trampers.png|thumb|right|300x300px|Nar Hida was one of many extras in ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones''.]]
The character Nar Hida first appeared as an unnamed extra in the [[2002]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], in the scenes aboard the ''Jendirian Valley''. The scenes aboard the ship were filmed in the art department depot of building 48 at [[Fox Studios, Sydney]].<ref name="365Days">''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]''</ref> The extra, in costume, was featured in the [[StarWars.com|Starwars.com]] [[Making Episode II Webdocs|Making Episode II Webdoc]] "A Twinkle Beyond Pluto,"<ref name="Twinkle">{{SW|url=video/a-twinkle-beyond-pluto|series=Making Episode II Webdocs|text=Part 5: A Twinkle Beyond Pluto}}</ref> which released before the film on [[July 31]], [[2001]].<ref name="ATBP Date">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/me2/archive.html|text=''Making Episode II Webdocs'' archive}}</ref>

===Databank entry===
In [[2006]], the character was named and expounded upon by [[Gregory Walker]], writing as NarbFlick, through the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]" In writing his winning [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry, Walker tied the character to the Baath brothers, who originated in [[2003]]'s ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]'' and had been used by Walker in his two previous winning "What's The Story?" entries, [[Magaloof/Legends|Magaloof]] and [[Acros-Krik]]. Unintentionally, a theme of criminality ran through Walker's winning "What's The Story?" entries, to varying degrees, with Hida, his final one, being the more noble of the three. He also created entirely new characters in Hida's unnamed daughter and wife.<ref name="blog" />

[[File:Whats_The_Story_entry_example.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Though the ''What's The Story'' feature (example pictured), Hida was named and expanded upon.]]
Walker was able to introduce other new elements to [[canon]] in writing about Hida, such as the planet Luptoom, which was later referenced in [[Nathan O'Keefe]]'s "What's The Story?" entry for [[Teyora Rekab]]. Originally, Walker had intended to have Hida attempt to rob Amidala and end up wounded by Skywalker, but he felt that Skywalker's [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] had been shown too much in previous ''[[Star Wars]]'' material, and was almost cliched. Instead he chose to have Hida rob a Bith passenger, but had originally included a segment of dialogue in his entry to augment the tale. The dialogue was eventually cut out by StarWars.com editors, to Walker's relief&mdash;he had felt that in straying from the standard Databank format, his entry would be disqualified. As such, he was surprised when it was chosen, and was happy with the compromise made by the StarWars.com staff.<ref name="blog" />
